title: U.S. Rig Count Holds Steady as Oil Production Hits Fifth Straight Record | OilPrice.com

The total number of active drilling rigs for oil and gas in the United States stayed the same this week, according to new data that Baker Hughes published on Wednesday ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. The total rig count in the US remains at 607, up 63 from this same time last year.

The number of active oil rigs rose by 1 to 470 during the latest reporting period, according to the data. This is 63 above this same time last year. The number of gas rigs fell by 1, which is 3 fewer than this time last year. Miscellaneous rigs stayed the same at 10.

The latest EIA data showed that weekly U.S. crude oil production hit a record for the fifth week in a row, rising during the week ending November 20 to 14.065 million bpd, up from 14.032 million bpd last week and up 251,000 bpd from a year ago.

Primary Vision’s Frac Spread Count, an estimate of the number of crews completing wells, rose during the week ending November 20, regaining 3 of the 4 crews it lost last week, settling at 194, which is up 15 year-over-year.

The number of active drilling rigs in the Permian Basin was unchanged during the reporting period, at 277. This is 26 rigs above year-ago levels. The count in the Eagle Ford stayed at 50, which is 11 more than this same time last year.

Oil prices were up on Friday prior to the data release, with Brent now trading at $94.28 (+3.15%) per barrel. WTI was also trading up on the day at $83.89 (+2.28%).
